arxiv-2605-10062: Edge computing over optical networks needs a dedicated simulation platform; GenioSim is novel and purpose-built. Carmine Cesarano, Alessio Foggia, and Roberto Natella build it. The 2026 paper is edge computing simulated at the speed of light. It simulates the optical edge.
plos-pone-0003462: Virologists traced bird flu's family tree in Vietnam in this 2008 paper. The genetic timeline helps predict which viral lineages pose the next threat to birds and people.
plos-pone-0003562: Immunologists found breast milk delivering living reinforcements in this 2008 mouse study. The work shows nursing passes more than antibodies: it transplants pieces of the mother's cellular immune education.
plos-pone-0003662: In 2008, a team found a heart-risk gene change that hits men only. A variant in gamma-secretase tracked with early clogged heart arteries in men, but not in women. The male-only link adds a sex-specific piece to why heart disease strikes some people decades early.
plos-pone-0003762: Leal and Ishida debunked a fire-ant myth in this 2008 paper. The negative result sends the search for the colony's chemical code elsewhere.
plos-pone-0003862: Back in 2008, a group mapped East Asia's genetic neighborhoods. Using genome-wide SNP arrays, Tian, Kosoy, and Lee charted population substructure across the region. The map helps gene hunters avoid false hits caused by hidden ancestry differences.
plos-pone-0003962: In 2008, Staiger, Machicao, and Schafer tied a new diabetes gene to insulin output. Variants in MTNR1B, a fresh type 2 diabetes risk locus, determined beta-cell function. The finding connects the melatonin receptor gene to blood-sugar control.
plos-pone-0004062: In 2008, Zarse and Ristow found antidepressants shortening worm lives. Mianserin and methiothepin raised body fat and cut lifespan in adult worms. plos-pone-0004162: In 2009, Jeong, Kwon, and Joo timed the worm's vanishing act. They traced the molecular time-course of dauer entry in C. elegans. Metabolic shifts marked the path into the hardy survival state. The timeline maps a masterclass in waiting out famine.
plos-pone-0004262: In 2009, Tamura, Sone, and Yamashita found support cells turning toxic. Glial expression of mutant ataxin-1 and huntingtin harmed neurons. plos-pone-0004362: In 2009, Kuhnen and Chiao found genes nudging risky money bets. Two dopamine and serotonin gene variants predicted money risk taking. The brain-chemical genes shaped gambling choices. The finding links brain chemistry to markets directly. The work opens money gene research.
plos-pone-0358762: Mustard farmers face a dilemma: too little nitrogen starves the crop, too much wastes money and pollutes. The results show higher yields, lower costs, and less environmental damage than blanket fertilizing.
plos-pone-0356062: Learning a second language lives or dies on vocabulary — and motivation may decide how many words stick. This study modeled the links between learners’ motivation, their vocabulary strategies, and the breadth of words they actually know. The structural model shows which motivational levers most powerfully expand a learner’s word bank.
plos-pone-0358362: Oligodendrocytes wrap nerve fibers in myelin — and when they die, diseases like multiple sclerosis follow. This paper found that Chromogranin B, a protein released by neurons, acts as a paracrine signal triggering oligodendrocyte death. Identifying this kill signal opens a new target for protecting the brain’s wiring.
plos-pone-0358562: Deep underground, tiny rock fractures whisper before they roar — but the signals drown in noise. This paper developed an automatic segmentation method for microseismic monitoring signals under low signal-to-noise conditions. Pulling clean events from the noise gives mines and fracking sites earlier warnings.
plos-pone-0355362: Aspergillus flavus makes toxins in food and resists drugs in clinics. This paper studied genetic diversity and antifungal susceptibility among ecological niche populations of the fungus in Yaoundé, Cameroon. The local data tell doctors and food-safety officials exactly which strains they are facing and which drugs still work.
plos-pone-0357662: China’s ‘One Village, One University Student’ project sends educated youth back to their villages. This paper tested whether rural talent cultivation enhances farmers’ social capital. The evidence shows whether the program truly weaves stronger community networks or just moves graduates around.
plos-pone-0357562: Does family shape how teens learn — and whether they cheat? This study tested family structure and family satisfaction as factors in adolescents’ autonomous motivation, cheating, and academic achievement. The findings untangle what home life contributes to school success, self-driven learning, and honesty.
plos-pone-0355962: Kaempferol, a flavonoid found in many vegetables, fights colon cancer — but only if it reaches the cell nucleus. This paper showed phase II metabolic enzymes and efflux transporters orchestrate kaempferol’s nuclear entry, suppressing colorectal cancer growth. The transport choreography reveals how to make this natural compound work harder as therapy.
plos-pone-0357962: Zambia urgently needs gestational age estimates — and AI-powered ultrasound could deliver them at the point of care. This pilot evaluation protocol will test implementing artificial intelligence-enabled obstetric ultrasound in Zambian clinics. The planned study brings accurate dating scans to low-resource settings that lack specialists.
plos-pone-0357262: High-power pulsed lasers machine aluminum alloys with extreme precision — when the physics is understood. This paper built a simulation model of pulsed-laser ablation of aluminum alloy and validated it experimentally. The model predicts exactly how the metal responds to each pulse.
plos-pone-0357462: How long should dual antiplatelet therapy continue after coronary stenting? This systematic review and network meta-analysis examined DAPT duration after percutaneous coronary intervention with contemporary drug-eluting stents. The synthesis gives cardiologists evidence-based guidance for one of their most common dilemmas.
plos-pone-0352262: Antipsychotic drugs may quietly impair how the female brain responds to insulin. This placebo-controlled, crossover neuroimaging study protocol will test the effects of antipsychotics on brain insulin action in females. The planned study probes a metabolic side effect medicine has largely overlooked.
plos-pone-0356462: Geriatric nurses face death daily — and their ability to cope shapes the care they give. This paper studied factors associated with death coping ability among geriatric nurses and developed culturally sensitive death education interventions. The interventions aim to sustain the caregivers who accompany life’s end.
plos-pone-0356762: Triple-negative breast cancer’s genetic drivers often hide from standard tests. This paper showed exome-based cancer driver gene comprehensive testing can provide a genetic diagnosis for these patients. The broader testing catches actionable mutations that narrower panels miss — opening doors to targeted therapy.
plos-pone-0356362: Childbirth at dangerously young or old ages persists in Bangladesh — but why? This paper used machine learning on the 2022 Bangladesh Demographic and Health Survey to uncover the determinants of high-risk age at childbirth. The ML analysis points policymakers toward the levers that actually shift maternal age patterns.
plos-pone-0356262: Feed additives can stabilize the rumen’s delicate chemistry in feedlot cattle. This paper tested selected additives’ effects on rumen pH dynamics, physiological responses, and rumen and cecum morphometrics in beef cattle. The findings help producers keep cattle healthy and growing on intensive grain diets.
plos-pone-0356562: Volleyball players’ patellar tendons take brutal punishment. This paper related patellar tendon micromorphology to body anthropometrics and lower-limb range of motion in volleyball athletes. The structural correlations help sports medicine understand whose tendons are built to survive the sport — and whose aren’t.
plos-pone-0355862: 3D-printed PMMA parts for medical use must have predictable hardness. This paper built machine learning models to predict the hardness of additively manufactured PMMA parts for biomedical applications. The predictive models let manufacturers dial in print settings for implants and devices that perform reliably.
plos-pone-0355462: International medical graduates in Canada face blocked pathways to practice — and some consider leaving medicine. This paper investigated who considers alternative employment pathways. The findings reveal the human cost of credential barriers — and the talent Canada wastes.
plos-pone-0355562: F-squares — a combinatorial design — meet cellular automata in this mathematical exploration. The paper investigated F-squares over cellular automata. The abstract findings enrich the theory of discrete dynamical systems — with potential echoes in cryptography and complex systems modeling.
plos-pone-0333162: Postoperative nausea and vomiting after spinal anesthesia — miserable and common — might be predictable. This retrospective study built machine learning models for that prediction. The ML models promise targeted prophylaxis — sparing low-risk patients unnecessary drugs while protecting the vulnerable.
europmc-pmc2845662: The nucleolus, the cell's ribosome factory, had never been mapped at the DNA level. This 2010 paper delivers the initial genomics of the human nucleolus. europmc-pmc2921362: A rare gene flaw brings sudden, scary swelling, and doctors needed one playbook. europmc-pmc2987762: A treatable dementia needs reliable diagnosis. This 2010 Japanese study shows brain-scan rules can spot normal pressure hydrocephalus. europmc-pmc3033362: The worm's brain wiring got mapped. This 2011 paper charts the roundworm's full neural wiring diagram. The authors reveal its design rules. Their work lights up the young field of connectomics. All 302 neurons made the map. Engineers borrow its wiring tricks.
europmc-pmc3040162: Cancer stemness runs on two pathways. This 2011 paper shows the Twist protein keeps cancer stem traits alive via two signals. The authors reveal the wiring. europmc-pmc3051362: Trauma, drugs, and PTSD intertwine. This 2010 paper studies drug use, childhood trauma, and PTSD in a city population. The authors reveal the tight tangle. europmc-pmc3059462: Whole plant extracts may beat single malaria drugs. This 2011 paper argues plant brews outdo lone compounds against malaria through synergy. europmc-pmc3070162: Germ needles got many jobs. This 2010 review covers the varied work of bacterial type IV secretion machines. The authors survey the tiny needles. Their overview aids germ science. The needles move DNA and toxins alike. Drug resistance rides these needles.
europmc-pmc6544462: Testicular cancer's classic blood markers miss many cases - but a tiny RNA called miR-371a-3p does better. europmc-pmc6567462: Most pancreatitis is mild, but 20-30% of cases turn severe - organs failing, intensive care needed. europmc-pmc6664762: A pig's gut microbes change dramatically from birth to market - and those shifts track growth. europmc-pmc6769762: Psoriasis turns skin into a battlefield - red, scaly plaques where immunity misfires. This review maps the risk factors: the genes, the immune triggers, and how T cells, dendritic cells, and skin cells conspire. Knowing the players points to better-targeted therapies.
europmc-pmc6770362: Most of our genome does not code for proteins - and some of that 'dark matter' drives cancer. This review surveys long non-coding RNAs in cancer development: how these RNA strands push tumors forward. The overlooked molecules are emerging as biomarkers and drug targets.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1162: Sticky notes on the fridge were not cutting it — GAO's 2007 report says Washington could teach homes far more about saving energy. openalex-w7204271762: Heavy bleeding after birth remains a top killer of mothers worldwide. arxiv-2606-16162: Decompilers turn machine code back into readable source code, but their output is usually rough and hard to follow. arxiv-2606-16362: Scan bots that read sick pics must earn trust — yet no one sees which specks sway them. This paper gauges each speck's pull with a sharp stats yard (Fisher scores), drawn per case. It hands docs and scan folk a true lens on bot calls.
arxiv-2606-16462: Brain-computer interfaces read EEG signals, but every person's brain patterns differ. arxiv-2606-16562: Do frontier AI models harbor bias against Muslims?
